values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/pinegrove ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Pine Grove State Forest Campground, Cheboygan: 6 sites, $20, managed by Otsego Lake SP 989-732-5485, 'Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Potable water from a free-flowing artesian well.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/pinegrove ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.'; 'Amenities include potable water from a free flowing artesian well.'), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/pinegrove ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Pine Grove State Forest Campground: 'Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 6 sites 'for tent and small trailer use' (the DNR's standard state forest wording; no maximum length posted). One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/pinegrove ('There are 6 sites for tent and small trailer use'; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (6 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Quiet, secluded rustic campground along the Pigeon River in Pigeon River Country State Forest, ~12 mi E of Wolverine via Wolverine Rd, Webb Rd and Campsite Rd; good High Country Pathway stopover. Carry-in boat access in the campground. Twisty/rutted dirt access road, but firsthand reviews confirm RVs make it in (direct river fishing access). --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: $20, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump/artesian well water, first-come only, 6 sites, 15-day max (all confirmed, derived -> manual). Boilerplate 'tent and small trailer' wording, silent on length. Season 'open all year' already manual, left. Type 'rustic', not equestrian; no ORV operation. DNR page silent on the access road's condition. Note trimmed of field restatements.
